title: Emergency Signs in Dogs and Cats
content: Emergency symptoms requiring immediate veterinary intervention include: severe arterial bleeding, severe difficulty breathing (dyspnea/open-mouth breathing in cats), collapse or inability to stand, unresponsiveness or coma, severe abdominal distension/bloat (GDV suspicion in deep-chested dogs), continuous seizures lasting over 3 minutes, pale or blue gums, suspected toxic ingestion (rat poison, chocolate, insecticides), severe dehydration, and prolonged labor (>2 hours between puppies/kittens). Keep the animal warm, calm, and wrapped in a clean blanket during transport to the nearest 24/7 veterinary hospital.

title: Cattle and Buffalo Anorexia & Digestive Care
content: Loss of appetite (anorexia) or indigestion (off-feed) in dairy cattle and buffaloes in India can stem from ruminal acidosis (excess green fodder/grain intake), bloat (tympanites), parasitic load, or foot-and-mouth disease (FMD). First aid measures: Provide clean fresh water, feed dry wheat/paddy straw, offer jaggery water with mineral mixture, and immediately consult a local Pashu Vaidya or Government Veterinary Hospital for rumen fluid analysis. Do not administer human painkillers or antibiotics without veterinary prescription.

metadata.source: Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying (DAHD), Govt of India

title: Avian Injury & Emergency Respiratory Protocol
content: In injured or sick pet birds (parrots, pigeons, budgies, poultry): Watch for fluffed feathers, sitting on the cage floor, tail bobbing while breathing, bleeding from blood quills or beak, or wing drooping. Keep the bird in a warm, dark, quiet box lined with paper towels (28-30°C). Apply gentle direct pressure with clean cotton for bleeding. Transport immediately to an Avian Specialist Veterinarian. Never use human ointment on bird feathers.

title: Vaccination Schedule for Dogs in India
content: Core vaccines for puppies in India: 6-8 weeks: DHPPi+L (Distemper, Hepatitis, Parvovirus, Parainfluenza, Leptospirosis) 1st dose; 10-12 weeks: 2nd booster; 14-16 weeks: 3rd booster + Rabies (Anti-Rabies Vaccine). Annual boosters required: 7-in-1 / 9-in-1 combo vaccine and Anti-Rabies vaccine. Rabies vaccination is mandatory under Indian law (Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act).

title: Goat and Sheep Vaccination & Deworming in India
content: Small ruminants (Goats and Sheep) in India require vaccination against PPR (Peste des Petits Ruminants), Enterotoxaemia (ET), Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD), and Goat Pox. Deworming should be performed biannually before monsoons (May-June) and post-monsoon (October-November) using broad-spectrum antihelmintics under veterinary supervision.

title: Dog Vomiting & Dehydration First Aid
content: Repeated vomiting in dogs can be caused by dietary indiscretion, gastroenteritis, viral infections (Parvovirus), or ingestion of toxic plants/foreign bodies. Immediate steps: Withhold food for 6-8 hours while providing small licks of fresh water or ORS solution. If vomiting continues for more than 12-24 hours, or if blood/bile is present, or accompanied by lethargy, seek immediate evaluation at a pet clinic or veterinary hospital.
